name: CIRCLES (Composed Image Retrieval for Causal Learning Example Selection)
venue: CVPR 2026 (IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition); preprint arXiv:2603.16737 (2026-03-17)
authors_affiliation: Guangzhi Xiong, Sanchit Sinha, Zhenghao He, Aidong Zhang -- University of Virginia
maintained_repo_url: https://gzxiong.github.io/CIRCLES/ (project homepage). N/A as a continuously-updated leaderboard/paper-list; the GitHub repo (https://github.com/gzxiong/CIRCLES) is the maintained code repo.
task_domain: Multimodal reasoning with vision-language models (VLMs): fine-grained image classification (CUB, Flowers) and visual question answering (OK-VQA, VizWiz), plus ScienceQA in the appendix. Framed as demonstration selection for visual in-context learning (ICL).
problem_setting: Offline, single-query inference-time in-context learning. A frozen VLM answers a query (image, question) conditioned on a set of retrieved in-context demonstrations drawn from a fixed training/demonstration corpus. Training-free (no retriever or VLM fine-tuning); CLIP encoders and the VLM are frozen. Single-agent, no interactive/multi-turn environment. Supervision is the labeled training corpus from which demonstrations (with their gold answers) are retrieved.
what_is_retrieved: Labeled demonstration examples (image, question, answer triples) from a VQA/classification corpus. Two complementary pools: (1) correlational similarity-based image neighbors, and (2) counterfactual-style demonstrations retrieved via attribute-guided composed image retrieval.
retrieval_grounding: STATIC external corpus -- a fixed labeled training/demonstration corpus K = {(I_j, Q_j, A_j)}; no growing or episodic memory written during deployment.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Fixed-budget top-k construction. The injected context is a fixed budget of 32 demonstrations, split 16 causal (composed/counterfactual) + 16 correlational (standard image-retrieval) examples; each pool is a TopK selection by a similarity score. Not framed as recovering a minimal complete set, but the paper does study budget allocation (breadth across attributes vs depth per attribute) under tight #CIR budgets.
cbr_cycle_coverage: [Retrieve] only. No Reuse-as-adaptation, no Revise, no Retain. Retrieved demonstrations are injected verbatim as ICL exemplars; the system neither adapts cases nor stores new ones.
explicit_cbr_grounding: False. The work does not frame itself as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner; it is positioned as counterfactual/causal demonstration selection for visual ICL via composed image retrieval, citing causality (Pearl-style do-intervention notation) rather than CBR.
retrieval_unit: Single demonstration (a complete image-question-answer example). Causal-pool items are demonstrations surfaced by matching counterfactual captions; correlational-pool items are nearest-image-neighbor demonstrations.
index_source: Static corpus, offline-precomputed. CLIP image embeddings z^I_j and text (question) embeddings z^Q_j for every candidate are precomputed once over the fixed training corpus; the store is frozen at test time.
index_structure_topology: Flat vector index over CLIP embeddings (L2-normalized image and text embeddings), scored by inner-product similarity; no graph or hierarchical structure.
retriever_type: Dense, off-the-shelf CLIP (ViT-g/14) embeddings used for cosine/inner-product similarity. Composed image retrieval is a training-free CIR pipeline (OSrCIR) where the VLM generates counterfactual captions whose CLIP text embeddings are matched against candidate image embeddings (LLM-as-query-generator + dense matching). Hybrid in the sense that causal retrieval combines image-caption similarity with question-question (text-text) similarity.
retriever_learning_signal: None (off-the-shelf). The retriever is a frozen CLIP model; no contrastive, LM-feedback, or RL training of the retriever. Demonstration selection is a fixed similarity ranking (top-k), augmented by VLM-generated counterfactual captions but with no learned retrieval policy.
query_construction: Two-track query construction. (1) Correlational: raw query image embedding z^I_q used for image-image similarity. (2) Causal: the VLM Phi extracts decisive attribute-value pairs from (I_q, Q_q), samples an alternative value v_i' for each attribute, and prompts the VLM to generate a counterfactual caption c^{do(a_i=v_i')} describing I_q under the atomic intervention do(a_i=v_i'); this synthetic caption embedding plus the query question embedding z^Q_q form the composed query. Score S_j = s^img (image-caption similarity) + s^txt (question-question similarity).
query_granularity: Task/query-level, one-shot at t=0. All retrieval happens once per query before answer generation (no per-step re-querying), but uses two-level signals: per-attribute counterfactual sub-queries are aggregated into the causal pool.
when_to_retrieve: One-shot. Retrieval is performed once per query (correlational + causal pools assembled up front), then a single VLM answer-generation call consumes the combined context.
retrieval_trigger_signal: Fixed schedule -- retrieval always runs once per query before answering; there is no confidence/uncertainty/learned trigger deciding whether or when to retrieve.
reranking: No explicit reranking stage in the main CIRCLES pipeline; selection is a single TopK by the combined similarity score S_j (causal) or s^corr (correlational). Note: the MMICES baseline does two-stage image-then-text reranking, but CIRCLES itself does not rerank.
retrieved_context_refinement: Light filtering via the scoring design rather than a separate refinement module: the question-question similarity term s^txt acts as a semantic constraint to prune counterfactual matches that are visually faithful but semantically off-topic. No decompose-recompose, distillation, or compression of retrieved items.
index_content_separation: N/A. Precomputed CLIP embeddings serve as a lightweight index while full demonstration content (image+question+answer) is loaded for injection, but the paper does not frame this as a progressive-disclosure index/content separation pattern.
dynamic_index_and_protocol: N/A (no tool index or external API/MCP integration).
how_retrieved_used: Prompt augmentation. The combined set R = R_causal U R_corr (32 demonstrations) is injected as in-context exemplars; the VLM generates the answer A_q = Phi(I_q, Q_q, R). Demonstrations are used verbatim (raw image-question-answer exemplars), with counterfactual examples implicitly teaching attribute->outcome causal contrasts.
planning_integration: One-shot exemplars at inference time (retrieve-then-answer). No planning, tree search, or multi-step acting; retrieval directly conditions a single answer-generation pass. No interleaving of retrieval with reasoning.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: Per-answer. All retrieval is completed before the single answer-generation call; retrieval is not woven into per-CoT-step or per-token reasoning.
adaptation_mechanism: Verbatim ICL exemplar (no case adaptation). Retrieved demonstrations -- both correlational neighbors and counterfactual examples -- are inserted as-is; CIRCLES does not rewrite or adapt cases. Causal benefit comes from contrastive composition, not adaptation.
retrieved_item_representation: Raw demonstrations: actual demonstration images paired with their questions and gold answers/labels, shown in-context. Counterfactual examples are real corpus images surfaced by synthetic intervention captions (not synthesized images).
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Single demonstration (raw exemplar). Counterfactual-style demonstrations expose attribute-level variations but are still concrete labeled examples, not distilled strategies, rules, or workflows.
noise_robustness_mechanism: Combined-pool design and a semantic constraint: pairing counterfactual (causal) demonstrations with standard correlational neighbors guards against spurious correlations; the question-question similarity term filters counterfactual matches that drift off the original query context. The retrieval-budget analysis (breadth-vs-depth across attributes) also mitigates imperfect CIR ranking. No retriever-aware training or self-reflection relevance evaluator.
memory_type: none -- static external corpus only; no episodic, skill-library, workflow, procedural, graph, or latent memory.
write_back: False. No new experiences/cases/skills are written back; the demonstration corpus is fixed and read-only.
online_growth: False. The retrievable store is frozen (offline precomputed embeddings); it does not grow during deployment/test time.
write_back_trigger: never -- nothing is written to memory.
failure_experience_usage: Success-only in effect: demonstrations carry their gold (correct) answers. There is no storage/retrieval of the system's own failed trajectories. Counterfactual examples surface contrastive class transitions (attribute change -> different correct label) but are themselves correctly-labeled examples, not failure records.
memory_evolution_update: N/A -- no memory is mutated (store is frozen, append-only changes do not occur during inference).
retrieval_as_learned_policy: False. Selection is fixed similarity top-k over frozen CLIP embeddings plus VLM-generated counterfactual captions; no learned/RL-optimized retrieval or case-selection policy.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: N/A / No. Single-agent, single-VLM inference; no memory or experience shared across agents or frameworks. (Method is evaluated across multiple VLM backbones independently, but no cross-agent sharing.)
benchmarks: CUB (Caltech-UCSD Birds-200-2011), Oxford Flowers, OK-VQA, VizWiz; plus ScienceQA (appendix). Backbones: Gemma3-4B/12B (and 27B in appendix) and Qwen2.5-VL-3B/7B; CLIP ViT-g/14 retrieval encoder.
benchmark_family: QA (knowledge-based VQA: OK-VQA; real-world VQA: VizWiz; multimodal science QA: ScienceQA) and fine-grained image classification (CUB, Flowers). Not part of the agentic web/embodied/tool/code benchmark families.
baselines: None (zero-shot, no in-context examples); Random (randomly sampled in-context examples); RICES (Retrieval-based In-Context Example Selection, image-image nearest-neighbor); MUIER (joint image-image + image-text multimodal retrieval); MMICES (two-stage: image-image candidate retrieval then text-image reranking). Appendix adds RICES* (compute-matched RICES with K=3 generations + self-consistency).
key_metrics: Classification: Accuracy (Acc) and weighted F1 (CUB, Flowers). VQA: Exact Match (EM) and word-level F1 (OK-VQA, VizWiz). Average computed by treating Acc as EM for classification and averaging EM and F1 across datasets. ScienceQA: test accuracy (%).
headline_result: CIRCLES consistently outperforms all example-selection baselines across four datasets and multiple VLM backbones, with average relative EM improvements ranging from 0.76% to 94.02% over the strongest selection baseline. Concrete example: on Gemma3-4B, average EM/F1 rises from RICES 58.71/64.54 to CIRCLES 63.54/68.53; on CUB (Gemma3-4B) accuracy 65.40 -> 71.97. Gains are most pronounced for small models and under information scarcity.
ablations: (1) IR vs CIR vs IR+CIR (Table 9, Gemma3-4B): CIR-only lags on fine-grained classification (CUB 25.16 vs IR 65.40) but is competitive on VQA; IR+CIR is best on all four datasets (+6-7 acc pts over IR on CUB/Flowers), showing complementary roles. (2) IR vs IR+Attr vs IR+CIR (Table 7): attribute text alone helps classification but hurts OK-VQA/VizWiz; CIR grounding gives the best overall, so attributes help most when grounded via counterfactual visual examples. (3) Question-question similarity term (Table 2): consistent OK-VQA gains (+5.16% to 14.32% relative EM), modest/robust on VizWiz; no effect on CUB/Flowers (identical question templates). (4) CIR implementation (Fig 5): OSrCIR > CIReVL by 5.39-5.56% relative accuracy. (5) Attribute quality (Table 6): dataset ground-truth attributes beat VLM-extracted by a modest margin (CUB Gemma3-4B 72.44 vs 71.97 acc). (6) Information scarcity (Fig 4): CIRCLES advantage over RICES grows as training data is removed (Gemma3-4B relative gain 10.05% at 0% removal -> 16.28% at 75% removal). (7) Retrieval budget (Fig 6): more #CIR helps; under tight budget spread interventions across attributes (breadth), with larger budget concentrate on fewer attributes (depth). (8) Compute-matched RICES* (Table 4): CIRCLES still wins, so gains are not just from extra generations. (9) IR similarity variants (Table 8): image-image+text-text gives small consistent VQA gains.
evaluation_decoupling: Partly. Primarily end-to-end task metrics (Acc/F1/EM). No standard intrinsic retrieval metrics (Recall@k/nDCG) are reported, but qualitative retrieval-quality analysis (diversity, counterfactual informativeness; Fig 3) and a retrieval-budget analysis are provided as proxies for retrieval behavior separate from final accuracy.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Mostly outcome-only (final answer Acc/F1/EM). Process insight is qualitative: case studies showing how counterfactual demonstrations expose decisive attributes and class transitions (Fig 3, Fig 7 failure/success modes), but no quantitative step-wise/process metrics.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: CIRCLES adds VLM calls (one attribute-extraction call + one counterfactual-caption call per selected attribute, plus the shared final answer call) but only ~10% token overhead vs RICES (Table 3: e.g., Gemma3-4B CUB 12.2k vs 11.1k tokens/question). A compute-matched RICES* (K=3 self-consistency) still underperforms CIRCLES (Table 4). Budget analysis (Fig 6) shows adding composed examples improves accuracy even at a lower total example count than IR-only.
context_budget_and_selection_count: Fixed budget of 32 in-context demonstrations for all methods (k=32); CIRCLES splits this as 16 causal (R_causal, composed/counterfactual) + 16 correlational (R_corr). Defaults in code: default_k=16, num_attributes=1, attribute_k=16. Budget-allocation ablations vary #IR, #CIR, and #attributes.
benchmark_construction_and_size: N/A (not a benchmark paper; uses existing datasets CUB, Flowers, OK-VQA, VizWiz, ScienceQA). [uncertain] exact test-set sizes used are not enumerated in the scraped text.
builds_on: RICES (Retrieval-based In-Context Example Selection; Yang et al. GPT-3 few-shot KB-VQA, Flamingo) for the standard image-retrieval / correlational component; OSrCIR (Reason-before-Retrieve one-stage reflective CoT zero-shot composed image retrieval) and CIReVL (Vision-by-Language training-free CIR) for the composed-image-retrieval module; CLIP for embeddings; Pearl-style do-intervention / counterfactual reasoning notation.
contrasts_with: Similarity-only / passive multimodal demonstration selection: RICES (image-image nearest neighbors), MUIER (image-image + image-text), MMICES (two-stage image-then-text rerank). CIRCLES argues these select correlated-but-non-causal examples that amplify spurious associations; it instead actively constructs counterfactual demonstrations. Also contrasts with CIR work that treats composed image retrieval as an end task rather than a tool for counterfactual demonstration construction.
lineage: Group A (ICL demonstration retrieval). Extends retrieval-based in-context demonstration selection from text/single-modality settings into multimodal VLM ICL, and introduces a causal/counterfactual selection objective (via composed image retrieval) rather than pure similarity ranking.
